solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ill-tempered animal crossing river

indicators.note: the animal is said to go across the river, so its letters sit on either side of it

parts.note: a moose is a large deer

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered beast wading across a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Morose means sullen and gloomy, a close synonym of bad-humoured.

clue.text: Note quiet mother's originally hesitant, confused state

parts.note: MI is a note of the sol-fa scale
SH is a call for quiet
MA'S is mother's, with the apostrophe ignored

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of hesitant

explanation.surface: A child notes their quiet mother is at first hesitant and bewildered.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishmash is a muddle or jumble, a confused mess.

clue.text: Spiteful, managed company on rise as alternative to our group

parts.note: ran means managed

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read upwards, so the letters are written backwards

parts.note: OR introduces an alternative
US is our group, ourselves

explanation.surface: A bitter remark: a firm was run as a rising rival to our team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on rise' turns OR into RO in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancorous means full of bitter resentment, a synonym of malicious.

clue.text: Without doubt churlish, full of energy

indicators.note: full of says the churlish word holds the energy letter inside

parts.note: surly means churlish, rude
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Undoubtedly that bad-mannered person is bursting with vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Surely is an adverb of certainty, meaning certainly.

clue.text: As coteries might be represented?

indicators.note: the letters of the word are represented in a new form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about how exclusive little cliques might be depicted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might be represented' rearranges COTERIES; at the same time a coterie is a small circle whose interests are understood only by its members.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric means understood only by a select inner circle, which is exactly how a coterie operates.

clue.text: Unexpectedly frail — sternest personal discipline the answer

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests things coming out in a surprising order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Surprisingly, strict self-control is the solution for a frail person.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-restraint is control of one's own impulses, a form of self-discipline.

clue.text: Two articles on time about plays

parts.note: THE and A are the definite and indefinite articles
RE means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Two pieces of writing on the clock, about stage drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre means drama as a whole, plays collectively.

clue.text: Archaic need to have odd items taken out where boats are?

indicators.text: to have odd items taken out
indicators.note: removing the odd-numbered letters leaves the second, fourth and so on of the two words

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned need to strip out oddments from where boats are moored.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhine is a great European river, a waterway full of barges and other craft.

clue.text: Inclined to talk in church? Indeed, about keeping off drink

indicators.note: about says the word for indeed goes round the teetotal letters

parts.note: AY is an old or dialect word for yes, indeed
TT means teetotal, abstaining from alcohol

explanation.surface: Gossipy in church? Yes, and staying sober too.
explanation.definitionFit: Chatty means talkative, given to easy conversation.

clue.text: Perhaps an address in Madrid

parts.note: an address here is a form of address, the Spanish title for a man, not a street location

explanation.walkthrough: 'address' tempts one towards a street or house; it is a polite title used when speaking to a man in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish equivalent of Mr or sir, used in addressing a man, so one example of a title in Spain.

clue.text: Performer upset Braille not available

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist is disappointed that a Braille version cannot be had.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like an emotional state of the performer, but it is the anagram signal, applied to Braille alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballerina is a female ballet dancer, one kind of stage performer.

clue.text: One using head maybe identifies poor player in field

parts.note: a butter is one who butts, using the head
to finger someone is to identify them, as to the police

explanation.surface: Someone who heads the ball points out a weak fielder.
explanation.walkthrough: BUTTER here is one who butts, not the dairy spread.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterfingers is the name for a clumsy fielder who drops catches.

clue.text: Maybe helping to make out way of working with acceptable books

parts.note: MO stands for modus operandi, a way of working
ON can mean acceptable, as in 'that's not on'
LIT is short for literature, books

explanation.surface: A method of working that uses suitable reading matter, perhaps to decipher something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make out' here means see dimly: moonlight helps you discern shapes at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A moonlit scene has enough light to discern things, so moonlight may assist in seeing them.

clue.text: Withdrawal of soldiers, pleasant surprise

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of British soldiers
a treat is an unexpected delight

explanation.surface: Troops pulling back turns out to be a welcome surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A retreat is a military pulling back, a withdrawal from a position.

clue.text: Second record — hard work

parts.note: a log is a written record, as a ship's log

explanation.surface: Setting a second record proves to be heavy going.
explanation.definitionFit: A slog is a long, tiring stretch of toil.

clue.text: Framework of lively debates with Duke involved

indicators.note: the duke is involved, wrapped inside the other letters
lively suggests energetic motion, so the letters of the word debates are jumbled

explanation.surface: The structure of spirited discussions in which a duke took part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lively' scrambles DEBATES to BESTEAD, and 'involved' puts D inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedstead is the frame of a bed, the structure supporting the mattress.

clue.text: For example roll-on, too darned odd

indicators.note: odd suggests something peculiar, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A roll-on, for instance, is just far too strange.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll-on is one kind of underarm deodorant, applied with a rolling ball.

clue.text: Greek with term for the ancient city's magnificence

parts.note: and means with, along with

indicators.note: term means the end, so the last letter of the word is taken

parts.note: Ur was the ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A Greek word for the splendour of an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'term for' takes the end of 'the', giving E.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandeur is splendour and impressiveness, a close synonym.

clue.text: Fighter rejected hints following anger

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word for hints is read backwards

parts.note: tips are hints or pieces of advice
ire is anger

explanation.surface: A boxer turns down advice after losing their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns TIPS back to SPIT. The Spitfire was a famous British fighter aircraft of the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spitfire was a single-seat fighter plane flown by the RAF.

clue.text: Indicate approval of popular Italian, genial (not half)

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable

indicators.note: not half says only the back half of the word genial is kept

explanation.surface: Approval for a well-liked, friendly Italian, only partly.
explanation.definitionFit: To initial a document is to sign it with initials, a sign of approval.

clue.text: Rise in peso a revelation

indicators.note: in says the answer is found inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: An increase in the value of the peso comes as a revelation.
explanation.definitionFit: To soar is to rise high, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Conclude with expected score, one might infer?

parts.words: with expected score, one might infer
parts.note: read as wordplay, W is with and RAP UP is PAR, the expected golf score, written upwards in a down entry

explanation.surface: Finish having hit the predicted score, presumably.
explanation.walkthrough: PAR is the number of strokes a good golfer expects on a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrap up is to finish or bring to an end, an idiomatic phrasal verb.

clue.text: Lag behind wife and daughter in valley

indicators.note: in says the wife and daughter letters go inside the valley

parts.note: a dale is a valley

explanation.surface: A man trails behind his wife and daughter on a walk in a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: To dawdle is to linger slowly and fall behind.

clue.text: Uproar as sale starts afresh (appointed leader ousted by resistance)

indicators.note: the sale gets a new start, its first letter replaced
ousted by says one letter is driven out and another takes its place

parts.note: an auction is a sale

indicators.note: leader points to the opening letter of the word appointed

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Commotion when a sale is restarted and the appointed head is replaced by opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: The A of AUCTION, matching the first letter of 'appointed', is replaced by R.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruction is a noisy disturbance or row, a synonym of commotion.

clue.text: Noisily eat meat Mike cut

indicators.note: Mike cuts into the meat, so its letter sits inside

parts.note: a chop is a cut of meat
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Mike cuts up his meat and eats it loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: To chomp is to munch noisily, chewing with vigour.

clue.text: US guy first of all is describing art houses, old and new

indicators.note: first of all takes the opening letter of every following word

explanation.surface: An American man describes art galleries, old and new.
explanation.definitionFit: An Idahoan is someone from the US state of Idaho, so an American man.

clue.text: Far-seeing, in favour of film presentation, say, by hospital department

parts.note: pro means in favour of
VID is short for video, an example of a film presentation
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A shrewd person backs showing a film beside a hospital unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Provident means planning for the future, showing foresight.

clue.text: Famous navigator, a flier

definitions.meaning: Sir Francis ..., the Elizabethan seaman who sailed round the world
a male duck, a bird that flies

explanation.definitionFit: Francis Drake circumnavigated the globe; separately, a male duck is a bird on the wing.

clue.text: Politician's influence, never ending, one noticed in job

indicators.note: one is seen within the job, so the following letters go inside it

parts.note: a post is a job

indicators.note: never ending says the final letter of the influence word is dropped

parts.note: pull is influence, as in having pull
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A politician's sway never fades, and he is noticed in office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'never ending' drops the last letter of the influence word, and 'noticed in' places that and the one inside the job word.
explanation.definitionFit: A populist is a politician who appeals to ordinary people against elites.

clue.text: Fellow before court, old, right bully

parts.note: HE, a male person, stands for fellow

explanation.surface: A man stands before an old court, rightly accused of bullying.
explanation.definitionFit: To hector is to intimidate with bluster, a verb synonym of browbeat.
